en: Draupnir - Ah, Your Highness Iyolin, you've returned. I have been worried ever since word came that you were stranded in Bifrost.
Iyolin - Grand Duke Mozel's kindness saw us through. And thanks to GS here, we crossed the Gigantes Mountains and made it back safely.
GS - They call me the Gray Scavenger.
Draupnir - Oh ho, a man with a remarkable face. May I ask where you come from?
GS - Forgive me for saying so, but I don't know where I come from myself.

GS - The truth is, I have no memory of my past. Four years ago a man named Anagi found me near death in the mountains of Bifrost. I was covered in wounds. Thanks to him I barely survived, but I lost every memory of my past.
Iyolin - What about the clothes you wore, or the things you carried?

GS - I had nothing of note, and my clothes were too badly torn to tell anything. After that I began working as a ranger in the Gigantes of Bifrost with Anagi, who was a retired ranger. The skills a ranger needs, like mountaineering, scouting and map-making, came to me naturally, so I picked up the work surprisingly quickly. I must have been a ranger before, or done something similar. Later, after Anagi passed away, I helped Grand Duke Mozel a few times and became fairly well known.
Draupnir - Hmm, a strange fate indeed. If you have nothing else to do, would you consider working for Dagal as a mercenary? For some reason, I feel I can trust you.
Iyolin - I agree. With the experience and skill you showed as a ranger on this journey, you would be a great help to our resistance.
GS - But I don't know how much help a ranger like me can be.

Draupnir - Not so. They say the Imperial Beradin is busy exploring ruins everywhere. It must be research into ancient civilisations and the gods, and we cannot simply stand by and watch. For that we need a capable dungeon explorer like you.
Rashid - Hehe, if it means being with you, I'm all for it!
GS - Hmm... Then I'll do my best, for whatever I'm worth.
